# Same SQL, Different Decision: Aggregate Risk Hides Cross-Lingual Instability in Text-to-SQL Verification

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#same-sql-different-decision)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://aclanthology.org/2026.oracle-main.6.pdf) · ORACLE workshop at EMNLP 2026 proceedings, printed pages 84–98

**Reading coverage:** All 15 pages: sections 1–9, limitations, appendices A–H, threshold/transport formulas, 23 tables, risk-coverage figure and worked candidate example.

## Research question

An English-calibrated verifier may execute different SQL candidates when only the question language changes, even if aggregate risk remains similar.

## Method

Generate SQL in English, hold candidate SQL/schema/database/execution label fixed and vary seven-language question renderings. Compare raw thresholds, language-aware score transport and translation-to-English while tracking candidate-level promotions and demotions.

## Evaluation

Two main 7–8B verifiers score 6,000 candidates; the primary database-disjoint test has 3,005 candidates. Thresholds and corrections are fitted on calibration databases. Clustered bootstrap intervals, repeated split sensitivities and literal-fidelity controls qualify the findings.

## What the results support

Similar ranking metrics and selective risk hide material execution-decision churn. Coverage matching does not restore candidate agreement. Pivot translation reduces several harms more than score transport, but its benefit varies by language, verifier and split and does not recover the English policy.

## Limits and qualifications

English is a reference policy, not truth. Execution labels are instance-specific; complete translation semantics were not manually verified. Generation and schema remain English. Qwen score saturation and precision sensitivity limit threshold transport; some small configuration comparisons are inconclusive.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

Adds decision-transition auditing to aggregate risk/coverage evaluation for multilingual abstention systems.
